heroHeadline: Esencia Developers Fire Back at Senate Days After Agencies Opposed the Project Bad Bunny Targeted Onstage
heroSubtitle: The fallout from Bad Bunny's Hiram Bithorn tour finale keeps rippling through Puerto Rico's government. Five days after the Aqueduct and Sewer Authority, the Electric Power Authority, and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company testified against the Proyecto Esencia megaproject in Cabo Rojo — the same project Bad Bunny demanded be "canceled" from the stage on August 22-23 and that thousands marched against in Cabo Rojo on August 23 — the Senate's Commission on Innovation, Reform and Appointments reconvened on September 1 and heard a sharply different case. Developer spokesman Roberto Ruiz Vargas said the now-$2.5 billion project would draw zero water or power from the public grid, relying instead on private wells, reverse osmosis, and a solar microgrid, while DRNA Secretary Waldemar Quiles Pérez said his agency's role is not to "promote or stop projects based on ideological criteria." Cabo Rojo's mayor struck a conditional note — "Cabo Rojo no está vendiendo su pueblo" — and Senator Eliezer Molina again disputed that the regional water system has capacity to serve the development. The hearing came days after a federal judge separately denied Bad Bunny $465,612 in legal fees despite his dismissed copyright win over Nigerian producer Dera and emPawa Africa.
